Like all candidates, Donald Trump benefits from what is known as earned media: news and commentary about his campaign on television, in newspapers and magazines, and on social media.
Earned media typically dwarfs paid media in a campaign.
The big difference between Trump and other candidates is that he is far better than any other candidate — maybe than any candidate ever — at earning media.
Trump earned $400 million worth of free media in February 2016, about what John McCain spent on his entire 2008 presidential campaign.

Paul Senatori, mediaQuant’s chief analytics officer, says that Trump “has no weakness in any of the media segments” — in other words, he is strong in every type of earned media, from television to Twitter.
Over the course of the campaign, he has earned close to $2 billion worth of media attention, about twice the all-in price of the most expensive presidential campaigns in history.
It is also twice the estimated $746 million that Hillary Clinton, the next best at earning media, took in.
Sen Bernie Sanders (I-VT) has earned more media than any of the Republicans except Trump.
